newsitem.title: USA: PLC Systems gets OK to expand heart study.
newsitem.headline: PLC Systems gets OK to expand heart study.

text.p: PLC Systems said on Wednesday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved an expansion of its clinical study of transmyocardial revascularization using its carbon dioxide heart laser.
The multi-center study, which tested the laser as the only treatment for end-stage coronary artery disease, was expanded to 300 patients at 20 sites, the company said.
The study had focused on only 225 patients at 15 sites, the company said. It said it petitioned the FDA for more sites because of growing patient demand for the procedure.
Transmyocardial revascularization uses the CO2 Heart Laser to create channels in the heart muscle, allowing blood to flow from the left ventricle to the oxygen-starved areas.

PLC Systems is a cardiac revascularization company developing medical systems to provide patients with coronary artery disease a third alternative or adjunct to angioplasty and cardiac bypass surgery.
